# Headline: does anything beat persistence? (generated by scripts/make_tables.py)

One row per experiment. A configuration beats persistence if the Diebold–Mariano statistic (HLN, Newey–West lag h − 1) is negative with p < 0.05 in every seed (one seed for the rolling rows), on the test windows, before any multiple-testing correction. MASE = MAE / MAE(persistence) on the same windows.

| experiment | seeds | forecast configurations | beat persistence, absolute loss | beat persistence, squared loss | lowest seed-mean MASE | configuration | evidence |

| rolling_origin_pooled | 1 | 36 | 0 | 0 | 0.998 | global_h1 tft | `results/rolling/rolling_table.md` |
| chronos_zero_shot | 3 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 1.031 | sudan_h30 chronos-mini | `results/chronos/chronos_table.md` |
| fx_target | 3 | 18 | 0 | 0 | 1.145 | sudan_h7 ensemble (FX route) | `results/fx_target/fx_table.md` |

**Total:** 231 forecast configurations; 0 beat persistence on absolute loss and 0 on squared loss.

Configurations overlap between rows (for example, the regime 'with' arm on the main split is the Phase 3 run), so the total counts evaluations, not distinct models.
